from.place: ## Proof, step (b) Essential surjectivity: algebraization through formal glueing, specifically the torsion-extension descent used in Proposition 05ER

title: Extensions by I-power torsion modules descend along a flat map that is an isomorphism mod I
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a flat ring map of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $I\subseteq R$ a finitely generated ideal such that the ring map $R/I\to S/IS$ induced by $\varphi$ is an isomorphism ($IS$ the ideal of $S$ generated by $\varphi(I)$). Let $N$ be an $R$-module and $Q$ an $R$-module that is $I$-power torsion (every $x\in Q$ satisfies $I^nx=0$ for some $n\ge1$). For an $R$-module $P$ and an $R$-linear map $u$ let $P\otimes_RS$ and $u\otimes_RS$ be the base changes [def-weil-module-base-change]. Let $0\to N\otimes_RS\xrightarrow{\iota}M'\xrightarrow{\pi}Q\otimes_RS\to0$ be an exact sequence of $S$-modules and $S$-linear maps. Then there are an $R$-module $E$, $R$-linear maps $j:N\to E$ and $q:E\to Q$ such that $0\to N\xrightarrow{j}E\xrightarrow{q}Q\to0$ is exact, and an $S$-linear isomorphism $\theta:E\otimes_RS\to M'$ with $\theta\circ(j\otimes_RS)=\iota$ and $\pi\circ\theta=q\otimes_RS$.

source.place: Dualizing Complexes, Lemma 05EH (lemma-neighbourhood-extensions, line 1502): for M I-power torsion the map Ext^i_A(M, N) -> Ext^i_B(M (x)_A B, N (x)_A B) is an isomorphism; stated here is the surjectivity for i = 1, with Ext^1 read as classes of extensions, the form in which the proof of More on Algebra Proposition 05ER (proposition-equivalence, more-algebra.tex line 24813), last paragraph, uses it

proof.text: Choose a surjection $p:P=\bigoplus_{j\in J}R/I^{n_j}\twoheadrightarrow Q$ with torsion kernel $K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-cyclic-presentation]. Write $k:K\hookrightarrow P$ for its kernel inclusion. Since $S$ is flat, tensoring gives the exact sequence $0\to K_S\xrightarrow{k_S}P_S\xrightarrow{p_S}Q_S\to0$ [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], where a subscript $S$ denotes tensoring with $S$. In particular $K_S$ identifies with the kernel of $p_S$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 05EG (lemma-neighbourhood-extensions, lines 24504-24516), reduction to a direct sum of $R/I^n$

proof.text: Pull the given extension $0\to N_S\xrightarrow{\iota}M'\xrightarrow{\pi}Q_S\to0$ back along $p_S:P_S\to Q_S$: put $T=\{(m,x)\in M'\oplus P_S:\pi(m)=p_S(x)\}$ with inclusion $N_S\to T$, $n\mapsto(\iota(n),0)$, and projection $T\to P_S$, $(m,x)\mapsto x$. This is exact: a pair in the kernel has $x=0$, hence $\pi(m)=0$ and $m=\iota(n)$ uniquely; for $x\in P_S$ choose $m$ with $\pi(m)=p_S(x)$. For each cyclic summand $C_j=R/I^{n_j}$, the pullback extension over $(C_j)_S$ descends by [lem-weil-pbc-cyclic-extension-flat-descent]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-direct-sum-extension-assembly] to these descents and obtain an $R$-extension $0\to N\xrightarrow{a}E_P\xrightarrow{b}P\to0$ and an isomorphism of extensions $\alpha:(E_P)_S\xrightarrow{\sim}T$, so $\alpha a_S(n)=(\iota(n),0)$ and $\operatorname{pr}_2\alpha=b_S$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 05EG (lemma-neighbourhood-extensions, lines 24510-24527): pullback of the extension and Ext compatibility with direct sums

proof.text: The pullback extension has a canonical lift of $K_S$: define $t_S:K_S\to T$ by $z\mapsto(0,k_S(z))$. It lies in $T$ because $p_Sk_S=0$, and $\operatorname{pr}_2t_S=k_S$. Transport it through $\alpha$ to $s_S=\alpha^{-1}t_S:K_S\to(E_P)_S$. Since $K$ is $I$-power torsion (step 1), [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-hom-flat-comparison] with target $E_P$ gives a unique $R$-linear $s:K\to E_P$ whose base change is $s_S$. The same Hom comparison with target $P$ is injective; after base change $b_Ss_S=k_S$, so $bs=k$. Thus $s$ is injective and its image meets $a(N)$ only at $0$: applying $b$ to $s(z)=a(n)$ gives $k(z)=0$, hence $z=0$ and then $n=0$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 05EG (lemma-neighbourhood-extensions, lines 24510-24517): six-term Ext reduction using Hom comparison 05EC; the splitting-lift diagram chase is written out

proof.text: Set $E=E_P/s(K)$ [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module]. The injection $a:N\to E_P$ remains injective after quotienting, by step 3, so it induces $j:N\hookrightarrow E$. The map $pb:E_P\to Q$ kills $s(K)$ because $pbs=pk=0$, and hence induces $q:E\to Q$. It is surjective since both $p$ and $b$ are. If $q([e])=0$, then $b(e)=k(z)$ for some $z\in K$ by exactness of $0\to K\xrightarrow{k}P\xrightarrow{p}Q\to0$; thus $b(e-s(z))=0$, and $e-s(z)=a(n)$ for some $n\in N$ by exactness of the $E_P$ extension. Hence $[e]=j(n)$ and $0\to N\xrightarrow{j}E\xrightarrow{q}Q\to0$ is exact.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 05EG (lemma-neighbourhood-extensions, lines 24510-24517): descending the extension from the presentation, quotient construction spelling out its six-term Ext reduction

proof.text: Flatness identifies $E_S$ with $(E_P)_S/s_S(K_S)$: tensor the exact sequence $K\xrightarrow{s}E_P\to E\to0$ and use [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact]. Under $\alpha$, the submodule $s_S(K_S)$ maps to $t_S(K_S)=\{(0,k_S(z)):z\in K_S\}\subset T$. The map $\operatorname{pr}_1:T\to M'$, $(m,x)\mapsto m$, is surjective because $p_S:P_S\to Q_S$ is surjective (step 1); its kernel is precisely $t_S(K_S)$, since $m=0$ forces $p_S(x)=0$ and $\ker p_S=\operatorname{im}k_S$. Therefore it induces an $S$-linear isomorphism $\theta:E_S\simeq T/t_S(K_S)\simeq M'$. For $n\in N_S$ its representative is $\alpha(a_S(n))=(\iota(n),0)$, so $\theta j_S=\iota$. For $[e]\in E_S$, the equality $\pi\operatorname{pr}_1\alpha(e)=p_S\operatorname{pr}_2\alpha(e)=p_Sb_S(e)=q_S([e])$ gives $\pi\theta=q_S$. This is the required isomorphism of extensions.

split_report.summary: The direct module proof of More on Algebra Lemma 05EG proves exactly the extension statement used by 05ER. Split it into presentation by cyclic ideal-power quotients (05E8), the torsion-source Hom comparison (05EC(2)), the cyclic quotient extension calculation (05EG via 05EE/05EF), and assembly over arbitrary direct sums (the detail 05EG omits). The item retains the pullback, splitting lift through Hom, quotient by the lifted kernel, and verification after flat base change. The derived Lemma 05EH remains a valid alternative source but is not used in this proof.

lean.statement: theorem exists_torsion_extension_flat_descent {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (_hflat : (algebraMap R S).Flat) (I : Ideal R) (_hI : I.FG) (_hquot : Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap (I.map (algebraMap R S)) (algebraMap R S) Ideal.le_comap_map)) {N : Type w} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] {Q : Type x} [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q] (_hQ : ∀ x : Q, ∃ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n ∧ ∀ r ∈ I ^ n, r • x = 0) {M' : Type y} [AddCommGroup M'] [Module S M'] (ι : S ⊗[R] N →ₗ[S] M') (π : M' →ₗ[S] S ⊗[R] Q) (_hι : Function.Injective ι) (_hιπ : Function.Exact ι π) (_hπ : Function.Surjective π) : ∃ (E : Type (max u w x)) (_ : AddCommGroup E) (_ : Module R E) (j : N →ₗ[R] E) (q : E →ₗ[R] Q), Function.Injective j ∧ Function.Exact j q ∧ Function.Surjective q ∧ ∃ θ : S ⊗[R] E ≃ₗ[S] M', θ.toLinearMap.comp (j.baseChange S) = ι ∧ π.comp θ.toLinearMap = q.baseChange S
